text:
anya: Hey, mkdocs linkcheck is failing for the 'Quick tips' page. The anchor generated for the heading with an inline emoji and a soft line break doesn't match the href used in the example snippet.

docs-bot: linkcheck failed: /docs/guide/quick-tips.md#quick-tips-emoji -> 404

anya: Example header:

```
## Quick tips ✨
- how to use the `cache-key` flag
```

When rendered the slug becomes `quick-tips-✨` on our preview build but linkcheck expects `quick-tips`.

ben: ah yeah, mkdocs/slugs can fold unicode differently. Two options: 1) add an explicit id on the heading (HTML comment) or 2) normalize the link to include the emoji slug. My vote: explicit id so links are stable.

sam: Proposed patch for quick fix (will open PR):

```
## Quick tips ✨ <!-- quick-tips -->
- how to use the `cache-key` flag
```

Also adding a unit in our linkcheck workflow to compare generated slugs from mkdocs and the raw anchor targets.

leo: I'll run a local build and verify. If that works, we should backport to the v1.4 release branch. @ben can you add a short note to the PR description about why we prefer explicit ids vs emoji-preserving slugs?

ben: yup, will add. Also documenting in the contrib guide (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) a short rule: 'Prefer explicit header ids for headings with non-ASCII chars or inline code.'

anya: thanks everyone. Sam, ping here when the PR is up and I'll merge once CI passes. :thumbsup:

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/472

docs-bot: CI started for PR #472 — running mkdocs build + linkcheck

docs-bot: CI passed ✅ — linkcheck fixed by explicit header id

anya: merged and backported to release/v1.4.1. Great catch, team :party:
